one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-29, before the open [15], two trading days before 2026-10-31. Consensus Q3 is about $9.85-9.96 EPS on $22.36B revenue, a sequential revenue dip from Q2's $23.0B that partly reflects Q2's one-time rebate-estimate benefit [19][18]. Full-year consensus of $88.46B revenue and $36.93 EPS already sits above the $85-87B / $35.50-36.50 guide [19][2], so the market expects another beat and raise. Lilly beat by about $2 a share in Q2 [16]. 2027 revisions have run 19 up to 4 down over the last 30 days [19]. The skeptic's offsets: Q3 is the first quarter with the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge ($50 copay, about $245 net), and Ricks said price 'will actually go down for sure' [35][37]. Foundayo is at roughly 47.5k weekly scripts against 183k for the Wegovy pill [22], so its line in the print could disappoint. A beat is the more likely outcome, but it is largely priced in; the risk is two-sided. I use a lognormal with median $1,156 (a slight positive tilt for the beat-and-raise pattern and the mild September drawdown) and a one-month sigma of 10.5%, a little above 35%/3.5 because of the print.

fair_value.method: A blend of three methods. (1) Horizon NTM EPS $50.75 (25% of a haircut 2027 EPS of $45.50 plus 75% of a 2028 EPS of $52.50) x 24x = $1,218, weight 0.5. (2) Consensus 2027 EPS $47.51 x 23x = $1,093, weight 0.3. (3) Morningstar's $980 DCF rolled forward 12 months = about $1,040, weight 0.2. Blended value: about $1,145, essentially today's price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon (Oct-2027) NTM EPS $50.75 x 24x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 EPS is $47.51 (range $40.73-54.94, 30 analysts) [19][20]. I take about 4% off for three reasons: (a) the Jan-2027 price reset (Novo Wegovy at a $675 list price [8], Medicare Bridge at about $245); (b) the oral launch lagging (Foundayo has about 20% of oral GLP-1 weekly scripts [22]); (c) Lilly's non-GAAP EPS absorbs acquired IPR&D (the 2026 guide absorbed $3.03/share [18]), and its deal pace makes $1-2/share of 2027 IPR&D likely while consensus cannot model unannounced deals.

+15.4% on $45.50, matching consensus 2027 revenue growth of 15.4% ($102.06B) [19]. That is a sharp slowdown from +28.6% EPS growth in 2027, reflecting the lower Medicare net price (Leerink: $245 is about 55% of current government net [9]) and ex-US generic semaglutide (India, Canada) [10][36].

Today's NTM P/E is about 25.6x ($1,149.85 / (0.25 x $36.93 + 0.75 x $47.51)) [19]. The 5-year mean is 34.6x and the industry 18.0x [4]. Morningstar's DCF implies 27x 2026 EPS [21]. Franke flags 23.7x 2027 as extreme versus Big Pharma [5]. I assume a modest de-rating to 24x as EPS growth falls from 29% to about 15%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Consensus 2027 EPS $47.51 x 23x (de-rated, near the skeptic benchmark)

inputs_detail.derivation: Franke's skeptic benchmark is 23.7x 2027 [5]. HSBC (Reduce, PT $940 since 10 Sep 2026 [16], $850 at the March downgrade [17]) implies about 20x. I use 23x: bear-tilted, but not HSBC's TAM-correction case.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Morningstar DCF fair value $980 (6 Aug 2026), rolled forward 12 months at about 8% cost of equity less a 0.6% dividend yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Morningstar raised it from $900 to $980 after Q2 on higher long-term margins plus a pipeline placeholder. It implies about 27x 2026 EPS. I use it as an independent cash-flow cross-check, since my own FCF base is distorted by capex.
About 8% cost of equity minus about 1.7% paid out as dividends and buybacks (H1-26 dividends $3.09B plus buybacks $3.96B on about $1.03T [12]) gives about 6%. 980 x 1.06 = $1,039.

inputs_detail.value: H1-26 FCF $10.8B (OCF $16.0B less capex $5.26B); about 2.1% FCF yield annualised
inputs_detail.derivation: This supports a cash-flow value below the P/E methods while capex runs near a third of OCF. Net debt is about $46B ($7.05B + $47.86B debt less $8.95B cash), about $51/share.

bear.story: The Jan-2027 US price reset (Novo $675 list price [8], Medicare $245 [9]) plus Foundayo stuck at about 20% of the oral market [22] and ex-US generic semaglutide [10][36] push 2027 EPS toward the $40.7 low estimate [19]. The multiple compresses to about 20x as growth slips into the low teens (HSBC's $80-120B TAM-by-2032 view [17]). A retatrutide label problem on dysesthesia or discontinuations [27] or a large IPR&D-heavy deal adds to it.

base.story: Volume outruns price, as it did in Q2 (US volume +37%, price -3%) [18]. 2027 EPS lands at $45.5-47.5, retatrutide is filed in Q1-2027 [38], and the multiple drifts from about 25.6x to about 24x NTM: roughly +5%.

bull.story: The Medicare Bridge drives a prescription inflection [35]. 2027 EPS tracks the top half of the range ($50+) [19] and retatrutide data underpin 2028+. The stock re-rates toward the Citi $1,600 and Berenberg $1,400 targets [38][34]: about $56 NTM EPS x 28x.

thesis_break_reason: About 24% below today, below the lowest Street target ($930 [20]) and near HSBC's original $850 [17]. Getting there in a non-crashing market would need the 2027 EPS consensus cut toward $40 (about 21x): evidence that US net price declines in the low-to-mid teens are outrunning volume after the Jan-2027 reset, or a genuine safety/label problem for tirzepatide, Foundayo or retatrutide. Credit (Aa3/AA-, positive outlooks [11]), the tariff exemption through Jan-2029 [28][29] and short interest of 0.84% of float [30] mean no balance-sheet or forced-flow path gets there on its own.

reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with about 30 more searches and fetches. The bear case is still about price and multiple, not solvency or fraud. Credit is pristine (Aa3/AA- positive [11]). Net debt is about $46B, about $51/share, and the H1-26 10-Q shows no accounting red flag beyond a normal growth-driven rebate-liability rise ($17.4B to $21.1B, with receivables up in line) [12]. Insider sales are small ($16M by execs in 90 days [16]) and the Endowment's are routine [13]. Short interest is 0.84% of float [30], and I again found no short-seller report. Corrections: HSBC's downgrade to Reduce was in March 2026 ($850 [17]), and on 10 Sep 2026 HSBC raised its target to $940 [16], so it did not drive the September dip, which was sector risk-off plus pricing worries [38]. The Foundayo liver risk is lower than I had it: ACHIEVE-4 showed no liver signal [26]. Tariff risk is neutralised through Jan-2029 by the MFN deal [28][29]. NAION has about 247 MDL cases across Novo and Lilly, with causation and preemption to be decided over the next year [24], so it is not material within the horizon. New skeptic evidence: (a) Lilly is losing the oral race, with Foundayo at about 20% of oral GLP-1 weekly scripts [22][23]; (b) FCF conversion is weak (about 2.1% FCF yield) because of capex and deal cash [12]; (c) Morningstar's DCF is $980 [21]; (d) non-GAAP EPS absorbs IPR&D, so the deal pace (three vaccine deals for $3.8B in May [31], plus Kelonia, Orna and others) is a recurring EPS tax; (e) retatrutide dysesthesia [27]; (f) 40% one-year discontinuation, though more than half restart [33]. On the other side, 2027 consensus is up to $47.51 with revisions 19 up / 4 down [19]. FY26 consensus sits above the guide. Berenberg upgraded [34], and the Street is 25 buys of 30 with a mean PT of $1,329 [20]. Net: fair value of about $1,145 (unchanged in substance) and a slightly higher scenario mean of about $1,215 (median about $1,155). The ladder is a mixture: 80% lognormal (median $1,190, sigma 30%) and 20% left-tail lognormal (median $1,000, sigma 40%), consistent with 35% realised volatility and a fatter downside for a price-reset/estimate-cut regime. Still unverified: prediction markets (Polymarket search returned no LLY market); Morningstar, Bloomberg and Benzinga pages blocked (details via search snippets); the Q2 call transcript, quoted via snippet only.
